title_zh: 藝術家與創作系列介紹
text_zh:
《萬物可愛論》是 Christy P 目前的核心創作系列，也是她將藝術、設計、品牌策略與人性觀察重新匯聚後，建立的第一個完整創作體系。

這段介紹從藝術家的成長出發：三歲，畫畫成為她的語言；十三歲，眼睛與淚水成為反覆出現的情緒符號；十六歲，藝術第一次成為能夠養活自己的專業。這些片段一起帶向她今天的觀看方法——可愛不是忽略矛盾，而是讓那些不容易被說出口的部分，得到另一種被看見的方式。
text_en:
EVERYTHING IS CUTE is Christy P’s current central body of work and her first fully developed creative universe, bringing together art, design, brand strategy, and observation of human nature.

This introduction follows moments in the artist’s development: at three, drawing became her language; at thirteen, eyes and tears emerged as recurring emotional symbols; at sixteen, art first became a profession through which she could support herself. Together, these moments lead to her present way of seeing. Cuteness does not erase contradiction; it offers another way for what is difficult to express to be seen.

text_zh:
Christy P 是現居高雄的台灣藝術家與跨域創作者，創作游移於繪畫、視覺設計與敘事建構之間。藝術家、品牌策略與設計工作者，並不是相互割裂的身分，而是她讓感受被準確傳遞的不同方法。

她把那些說不出口的感受，變成顏色。神情平靜的女孩、不對稱的眼睛與黑色陪伴者，構成一個看似童真、卻具有心理張力的世界。她關注的不是把人簡單劃分為好或壞，而是觀看那些彼此矛盾、卻同時存在的內在面貌。
text_en:
Christy P is a Taiwanese artist and interdisciplinary creator based in Kaohsiung. Her practice moves between painting, visual design, and narrative construction. Artist, brand strategist, and designer are not separate identities so much as different ways of communicating feeling with precision.

She turns what cannot be spoken into color. Composed girls, asymmetric eyes, and black companion creatures form a world that appears playful yet carries psychological tension. Rather than dividing people into good or bad, her work attends to the contradictory inner selves that coexist within us.

title_zh: 三歲，畫畫成為她的語言
title_en: AGE THREE — DRAWING BECAME HER LANGUAGE
text_zh:
「還不懂得為自己辯解以前，她已經先學會了畫畫。」

三歲的這一頁，將繪畫放在語言之前。對 Christy P 而言，畫畫很早便成為理解自己與世界的方法：當感受還無法被清楚說明，線條與顏色已經可以承接它們。這並不是一段完整的求學履歷，而是她創作起點的一個重要片段。

圖中的女孩手持畫筆，黑色陪伴者安靜地待在身旁；月亮、皇冠與鮮明筆觸，把成長經歷轉化為她今天的視覺語彙。從這裡可以看見，畫畫不只是表現技巧，也是一種表達與認識自己的方式。
text_en:
“Before she learned to explain herself, she had already learned to draw.”

This page places drawing before spoken explanation. For Christy P, painting became an early way of understanding herself and the world. When a feeling could not yet be clearly expressed, lines and colors could already hold it. This is a significant moment in her creative beginnings, rather than a complete account of her education.

The girl holds a brush while a black companion stays quietly beside her. The moon, crown, and vivid painted marks translate that early experience into the artist’s present visual vocabulary. Drawing is presented not only as a skill, but also as a way of expressing and recognizing oneself.

text_zh:
「在近乎軍事化的要求裡，她學會察言觀色，也學會把自己的情緒收好。」

十三歲的這一頁，呈現觀看他人與隱藏自己的雙重經驗。眼睛與淚水在青少年時期反覆出現在 Christy P 的作品裡，逐漸成為情緒、凝視與自我保護的視覺符號。眼睛既是理解世界的入口，也承載著希望被理解的願望。

圖中女孩神情平靜，桌面上卻散落著眼睛與淚水的畫稿；表面的安靜與畫面裡的情緒，形成微妙張力。「那些眼睛，在等世界看見她。」這段經歷讓人理解，她筆下的淡定並不等於沒有感受，而可能是一種把感受暫時收好的方式。
text_en:
“Raised under nearly military discipline, she learned to read every expression—and hide her own.”

This page brings together two experiences: watching others closely and keeping one’s own emotions contained. During adolescence, eyes and tears became recurring motifs in Christy P’s work, gradually developing into visual symbols of emotion, perception, and self-protection. Eyes offer a way to understand the world while also holding a wish to be understood.

The girl appears composed, yet drawings of eyes and tears lie across the table. That contrast creates tension between outward quiet and inward feeling. “Those eyes were waiting for the world to see her.” The page suggests that composure is not the absence of emotion; it may be a way of keeping emotion safely within.

title_zh: 十六歲，繪畫第一次養活了她
title_en: AGE SIXTEEN — ART BECAME A WAY FORWARD
text_zh:
「十六歲，藝術成為她第一個能夠養活自己的專業。」

在這個階段，繪畫從表達感受的方法，進一步成為她走進世界的能力。它不再只是讓情緒有所出口，也成為一條可以向前走的路：感性經驗開始與專業、生活和自主選擇相連。

女孩一手握著畫筆，一手拿著硬幣，身旁陳列著小幅畫作與黑色陪伴者。這些元素把創作與生活並置，讓「靠藝術養活自己」不只是一句抽象描述。畫筆與硬幣，也讓人看見藝術如何開始與自主生活相連：一個原本替感受找到出口的方法，逐漸成為支持生活的專業。
text_en:
“At sixteen, art became the first profession that allowed her to support herself.”

At this stage, painting grew from a means of expressing feeling into an ability through which she could enter the world. It was no longer only an emotional outlet; it became a way forward. Artistic experience began to connect with professional work, everyday life, and independent choices.

The girl holds a brush in one hand and a coin in the other. Small pictures and a black companion appear beside her, bringing creativity and livelihood into the same scene. The brush and coin also connect art with independent living: what first gave feeling an outlet was becoming a profession that could sustain everyday life.

text_zh:
「沒有任何事物只有善或惡，每一種存在，都有它可愛的一面。」

《萬物可愛論》凝視人們習慣隱藏的部分——慾望、嫉妒、孤獨、恐懼與愛。女孩、黑貓、兔子、怪物、皇冠與花朵，讓這些情緒不只以抽象概念存在，而成為可以被觀看的角色與畫面。看似童真的形式，承接著複雜的人性。

在這個系列裡，「可愛」不是裝飾，也不代表純真或無害。它是一種越過第一印象的觀看方法，讓柔軟與矛盾同時被看見。理解不等於合理化傷害，親近也不意味著放棄界線。第一季共有十二件作品；目前 LINE 已收到並設定前十件的圖文導讀。
text_en:
“Nothing is purely good or evil. There is a cute side to everything.”

EVERYTHING IS CUTE turns toward what people tend to hide: desire, envy, loneliness, fear, and love. Girls, black cats, rabbits, monsters, crowns, and flowers give these emotions a visible presence. What appears playful holds the complexity of human nature.

In this series, cuteness is neither decoration nor a guarantee of innocence or harmlessness. It is a way of looking beyond first impressions so that tenderness and contradiction can be seen together. Understanding does not justify harm, and closeness does not require abandoning boundaries. Season one comprises twelve works; images and bilingual readings for the first ten are currently available in this LINE account.

title_zh: 我只是看見了它可愛的那一面
title_en: I SIMPLY SEE THE CUTE SIDE OF IT
text_zh:
「我不是把世界變得可愛，我只是看見了它可愛的那一面。」

這張圖卡收束了藝術家與系列的介紹。它不是宣稱世界沒有黑暗，而是說明 Christy P 選擇如何觀看世界：不把慾望、嫉妒、孤獨或恐懼簡單排除在理解之外，仍然看見其中的柔軟、矛盾與需要被辨認的情緒。

《萬物可愛論》是她的第一個正式創作系列，也是一套觀看的方法。圖中女孩與黑色陪伴者一同望向帶有月亮、星星與城市的世界；畫面可被讀作邀請觀者跨過第一印象，再多看一面。這份觀看仍然保留界線：看見可愛，不代表否認傷害。
text_en:
“I don’t make the world cute. I simply see the cute side of it.”

This card brings the artist and series introduction to a close. It does not claim that the world contains no darkness. It explains how Christy P chooses to look: desire, envy, loneliness, and fear are not simply excluded from understanding. Their tenderness, contradictions, and emotional complexity remain worth noticing.

EVERYTHING IS CUTE is her first formal series and also a way of seeing. The girl and black companion look toward a world of moons, stars, and a city. The scene can be read as an invitation to move beyond a first impression and look at another side. That invitation still preserves boundaries: seeing cuteness does not mean denying harm.
